wizard.question.app_template.example: Example: a web application for managing bookings.
wizard.question.app_template.help: Choose the template that best describes the application's primary surface.
wizard.question.app_template.option.api_: Example: an API for querying and updating inventory.
Choose this option when the primary product is an API consumed by other systems.
wizard.question.app_template.option.auto: Example: a process that reconciles invoices every night.
Choose this option when the primary product automates a workflow or task.
wizard.question.app_template.option.web_: Example: a web portal for customers and internal staff.
Choose this option when people will use the product mainly through a browser.
wizard.question.assistance_level.example: Example: show explanations only when requested.
wizard.question.assistance_level.help: Indicate how much detail the Wizard should provide while gathering decisions.
Example: explain an option when its help is opened.
Shows brief help when it is relevant or requested.
Example: accompany every question with context and consequences.
Shows comprehensive explanations throughout the journey.
wizard.question.data_sensitivity.example: Example: personal customer data subject to a retention policy.
wizard.question.data_sensitivity.help: Classify the most sensitive data the application will handle.
Example: procedures and metrics available only to staff.
Choose this option for internal information that must not be published.
Example: customer names, email addresses, and preferences.
Choose this option when data relates to identified or identifiable people.
Example: a product catalog published without restrictions.
Choose this option when the data may be disclosed publicly.
Example: health records or regulated financial data.
Choose this option when laws or industry standards impose specific controls.
wizard.question.inference_mode.example: Example: deterministic rules with optional assistant suggestions.
wizard.question.inference_mode.help: Indicate whether the Wizard may use inferential assistance when proposing answers.
wizard.question.inference_mode.option.as: Example: suggest a classification for the person to confirm.
Allows assistant suggestions without turning them into automatic decisions.
wizard.question.inference_mode.option.de: Example: derive the next question only from confirmed answers.
Uses only reproducible rules and explicit answers.
wizard.question.objective.example: Example: reduce customer onboarding time without losing traceability.
wizard.question.objective.help: Describe the outcome the application must achieve and how success will be recognized.
wizard.question.quality_profile.example: Example: high assurance for a workflow that handles regulated data.
wizard.question.quality_profile.help: Choose the level of rigor required for testing, evidence, and operations.
wizard.question.quality_profile.option.h: Example: strengthened controls and independent evidence for every release.
Choose this option when failure has critical consequences and stronger evidence is required.
wizard.question.quality_profile.option.r: Example: traceability and controls required by an industry standard.
Choose this option when the product must meet explicit regulatory obligations.
wizard.question.quality_profile.option.s: Example: automated tests and routine review before release.
Choose this option for a product with customary quality controls.
wizard.question.work_mode.example: Example: extend an existing application while preserving its contracts.
wizard.question.work_mode.help: Indicate whether an application will be created or an existing one will be changed.
wizard.question.work_mode.option.create_: Example: start a new application from its confirmed requirements.
Choose this option when there is no existing codebase to preserve.
wizard.question.work_mode.option.work_ex: Example: add a capability to an existing repository.
Choose this option when existing code, contracts, or decisions must be respected.
